data.name: Mikael
data.gender_notes: Mikael is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Mikael means ‘who is like God?’. It is derived from the Hebrew words ‘mi’ meaning ‘who’ and ‘kahal’ meaning ‘God’. The name was popularized in Christian tradition due to the archangel Michael. The name Mikael carries the meaning “Who is like God?” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Mikael usually hope their child will grow to embody who is like god? and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine protection and strength.
data.etymology: Mikael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Who is like God?.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mikael total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_latin.name: Michael

in_english.name: Mikael
in_english.long_meaning: Mikael is derived from the Hebrew name Michael, meaning who is like God, and is considered a powerful archangel in Christian tradition, known for his strength and protection, and is often associated with courage and leadership

data.cultural_impact: Mikael is most famously known as the name of the archangel Michael in Christian tradition. He is often depicted as the leader of God's army and a protector against evil. The name gained widespread popularity among Eastern Europeans and is now commonly used in many Christian countries.
data.spiritual_significance: Mikael is a powerful name with deep spiritual meaning. It serves as a constant reminder that we are all created in the image of God and that we have the capacity to be like Him. The name symbolizes the ultimate aspiration of every human being – to live a life that is pleasing to God and to reflect His divine qualities. It is a call to strive for greatness and to seek God's guidance in all things.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mikael, meaning "Who is like God?" in Hebrew, symbolizes the profound faith and trust in God's supremacy and all-encompassing power. It's a reminder of God's presence and protection, and the unwavering belief that only He is worthy of praise and reverence.

biblical_reference.note: Michael is mentioned as a protector of Israel and a leader of the archangels

historical_references.reference: Mikael the Archangel is mentioned in the Old Testament as 'Mikha'el', the 'who is like God', and believed to have led God's army against Satan and his angels during the war in heaven.
In the New Testament, Mikael is named as the angel who appeared to the shepherds in Bethlehem and announced the birth of Jesus Christ.
